`budgets` is a ratchet: the gate fails if a category exceeds its budget, so the debt can only
shrink. Lower a budget in the same commit that removes entries, to lock the gain in.
Budgets count bypass CALLS, not entries. `calls` on an entry declares how many bypass calls
that member holds (default 1); the gate fails if the real count differs in either direction.
Without that, a member already on this list could absorb further bypasses silently.

libs/features/document-detail/src/lib/do.residualRisk: SCHEME IS VALIDATED, ORIGIN IS NOT. There is deliberately no origin allow-list here: a customer configures where their own ARender lives, so the allowed origin is not knowable to us (unlike loadPreviewFallback, where it must be the Nuxeo repository). What is closed is the privilege ESCALATION — javascript: becoming script execution in our own origin, with our session and DOM. What remains is inherent to the feature: whoever can edit the app-config manifest can point this iframe at any https origin. Accepted because (1) a third-party https origin in an iframe is a separate browser origin with no access to our DOM or cookies, so it is not an escalation; (2) the manifest is already a trusted Layer 0 customer surface that controls far more than this; (3) the correct control is a CSP frame-src response header, which no manifest editor can override — and NONE IS CURRENTLY SET, which is worth a ticket. NOT covered: any defect letting an untrusted party write the manifest.
libs/features/document-detail/src/lib/do.justification: MITIGATED FOR THE ESCALATION. The trusted string is `${cfg.viewerOrigin}/?url=…` and viewerOrigin comes from the customer-editable app-config manifest, so `javascript:alert(1)` there became script execution in this app's origin — a complete, non-blank, new URL()-parseable value that no completeness check catches. Now validated twice, both failing closed to null: ARenderService treats a viewerOrigin that is not an http(s) origin (https unless isDevMode) as unconfigured, so the dangerous URL is never built; and this member re-validates with navigableUrlOrNull before trusting, because a privilege boundary defended in exactly one place is one refactor from undefended. Rejection tests: arender.service.spec.ts (5 schemes, plus the production-http branch forced via ngDevMode) and document-detail.viewer.spec.ts (4 schemes) — all confirmed red with the guards removed. See residualRisk above before reading this as complete.
